summary: Built in 1938 by the Alabama Forestry Commission; a structure stopped at 60 feet with an unusual 14x14 ft cab, per the National Historic Lookout Register.

facts.design: Sloped-leg tower with a 14x14 ft cab made of two 7 ft metal sections on each side

events.note: Register's Built field; Alabama Forestry Commission builders stopped at 60 feet
Registered January 27, 2010 on nomination by Madeline Hildreth

corrections.why: The register describes sloped legs carrying a cab, which is a tower

evidence.supports: built 1938 by Alabama Forestry Commission; builders stopped at 60 feet
evidence.quote: Constructed in 1938, the Alabama Forestry Commission builders stopped at 60' where the sloped legs measured 14'x14' at the top, instead of 90' where a 7'x7' cab would be mounted.

evidence.supports: cab of two 7-foot sections on each side, unique
evidence.quote: Two 7' wide sections of a metal cab were joined on each of the four sides creating a unique 14'x14' cab.

evidence.supports: no other lookout cab like it among 900+ listings
evidence.quote: There is no other lookout cab like Underwood Lookout Tower in the 900+ listings on the NHLR.
Location East Brewton Escambia County, Alabama

evidence.supports: probably fewer than 75 historic lookouts still standing in Alabama
evidence.quote: Today, however, there are probably less than 75 of these historic structures still standing in Alabama.

evidence.supports: many are very unsafe and illegal to climb
evidence.quote: Many are looking worse for the wear, are very unsafe, and are illegal to climb.

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann: Keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: One register page carries the design, build year and registration details. Correction proposed: kind 'unknown' to 'tower', for editor review. height_m 18.3 is the register's 60-foot figure where the legs stop; confirm whether that is the cab floor. The register does not state status, condition or access. No staffing or fire records found. A Michigan page titled 'Underwood Hill' in the eastern lookouts cache is a different site and was not used.
